title: 2002 AMC 8 Problem 24
statement: Miki has a dozen oranges of the same size and a dozen pears of the same size. Miki uses her juicer to extract \(8\) ounces of pear juice from \(3\) pears and \(8\) ounces of orange juice from \(2\) oranges. She makes a pear-orange juice blend from an equal number of pears and oranges. What percent of the blend is pear juice?

solutions.text:
Use \(6\) pears and \(6\) oranges, which is an equal number of each fruit.

Since \(3\) pears make \(8\) ounces, \(6\) pears make \(16\) ounces. Since \(2\) oranges make \(8\) ounces, \(6\) oranges make \(24\) ounces.

The blend has \(16+24=40\) ounces total, of which \(16\) ounces is pear juice. The pear-juice percent is \(\frac{16}{40}=40\%.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Use an equal convenient number of pears and oranges.
Six pears and six oranges make both juice amounts easy to compute.
